description: We’re Orbitrace, four students passionate about physics, aerospace and AI. For NASA’s Flame in Freefall challenge, we built AETHER-BURN X, an interactive platform that explores NASA microgravity combustion research, compares experimental conditions and investigates spacecraft fire-safety scenarios. Our evidence-grounded research assistant traces findings to scientific sources, flags uncertainty and identifies research gaps. We welcome skills in computational physics, Python, ML and UI/UX.
summary:
AETHER-BURN X : The evidence-based scientific intelligence platform Team Orbitrace developed to meet the requirements of NASA’s "Flame in Freefall" challenge. Here, fragmented research on microgravity combustion is being transformed into a user-interactive system that allows for in-depth investigations of possible scenarios regarding fire safety on space missions.

The experiments performed by NASA are combined with visualizations of scientific data, scenario analysis, and a source-referenced research assistant. Users can configure a variety of parameters such as oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow and gravity as well as define material properties in order to search for specific results of interest to them, compare experiments and find limitations of already done research.

It differs from typical research dashboards in that AETHER-BURN X also assesses the relevance of the experimental results for the respective scenario. The scientific verification system of AETHER-BURN X traces back conclusions to their sources, makes a distinction between observations and modeled results and indicates in each case if statements are unsupported.

This improved access, comparison, and transparency of relevant data is meant to assist research in better informing the investigation of space-related fire incidents as well as help to uncover many of the open questions relevant to future human space exploration such as that required for habitats on the moon.
details:
AETHER-BURN X: Evidence Before Inference

What It Does and How It Works
Exploring NASA’s Fire Research
AETHER-BURN X is a web-based workbench for research, specifically developed for the Flame in Freefall challenge by NASA. This research workbench enables researchers, students as well as casual users of the web to explore NASA’s microgravity work on combustion. Different reports, experimental tables as well as literature are loaded with relevant evidence and integrated in a command center to help users in investigating scenarios of interest, to show them relevant results and to help them in finding missing parts for additional experiments.

From Scenarios to Sources
Specific experimental conditions (oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, material) can be selected to investigate corresponding evidence. The sources can be opened in a drawer to access corresponding documents. The Drawer contains the identified research gap and the corresponding experimental design for missing evidence. The five-step walkthrough introduces the major tools for research on AETHER-BURN X.

A Real Experimental Example
Our experimental set up currently consists of 129 verified experimental results from the experimental results section of the BASS-II technical report (NASA/TM-20210011385), plus 82 metadata entries from relevant NASA NTRS literature.

A 0.1 mm PMMA film is used with an initial oxygen level of 22.2% (measured before experiment) and an airflow rate of 5 cm/s (measured during experiment). Airflow is discontinued halfway through the film’s length when the flame front has reached that point. The flame then rapidly extinguishes. This experiment is preserved and can be viewed in the “Report’s” section of the workbench in order to provide users with the most accurate information possible for their interpretation of the provided results.

Benefits and Intended Impact
Making Research More Accessible
The purpose of AETHER-BURN X is to facilitate access to all of the available evidence, to enable researchers and students alike to compare and trace any lines of research and, where appropriate, to assess the conditions of the individual experiments in order to draw conclusions regarding the wider relevance of the findings and how they may have been affected by specific experimental circumstances.

Supporting Future Experiments
It will lead to more informed questions and better preparation for future experiments by making visible all the existing and missing information.

Tools and Technologies
Development and Data Processing
We implemented this project in Python and developed a web application using the Django framework to create the web application. SQLite is used as a metadata store for the structured metadata, while Parquet and DuckDB are used for analytical data access. We used Pandas, NumPy, and SciPy for the data processing and the associated scientific calculations.

Interface and Visualizations
We use HTMX with Alpine.js for interface interactions. Plotly is used for all of our interactive visualizations within the core application. This can all be run locally post-setup (no API key / internet connection required for core app).

What Makes the Project Creative
Connecting Evidence to Next Steps
When we thought of innovating around an Evidence-Based Research Assistant, we thought about how we can link exploring scenarios with finding the relevant sources for said scenario, comparing said sources, planning corresponding experiments and then running said experiments.

An Evidence-Based Research Assistant
The research assistant uses a deterministic retrieval method and then verifies numeric claims with corresponding citations to produce fully inspectable answers based on empirical evidence.

Factors Our Team Considered
Scientific Honesty
All fields (even those of value 0.0) are reported as missing if they were not filled in by report authors. A single record is reported as a verified summary, distinct from an unverified summary. All calculations, along with corresponding model output(s), are clearly differentiated from metadata and corresponding NTRS full-text coverage.

Meaningful Comparisons
Also were considered factors, which in comparison of experiments influence such as the material, the configuration of the tested piece, the gravity and the flow of air. An individual experiment does not warrant to be considered as a safe threshold for other applications.

Accessibility and Responsible Use
For new users, first time in the AETHER-BURN X app, guidance is provided to allow them to research the required information even without prior knowledge of the functionality of the app. AETHER-BURN X supports research and also studies, but it does not certify any given spacecraft to be safe for any given conditions.
